properties.name: OpsTechPro
properties.description:
OpsTechPro is a hospitality technology company developing AI-powered platforms that transform how hotels operate, communicate with guests, and manage assets across entire portfolios. Our mission is to bring operational intelligence to hotel management by connecting guest communication, daily operations, preventive maintenance, and capital planning into one integrated ecosystem.

The OpsTechPro platform consists of three powerful solutions that can operate independently or together through a unified single sign-on environment:

OpsTechPro AI – An operational management platform that helps hotels manage work orders, preventive maintenance, inspections, compliance, and asset performance. Built-in AI intelligence analyzes operational data and provides portfolio-level reporting and insights that help leadership identify trends, risks, and opportunities to improve efficiency.

Guest Voice AI – An AI-powered guest communication platform that automatically converts guest messages and requests into operational tickets and routes them to the appropriate department. The system confirms task completion with the guest, collects real-time satisfaction feedback, and reduces manual coordination for front desk teams.

Hotel CapEx AI – A capital planning platform that connects operational repair history with asset budgeting. By analyzing equipment performance and maintenance costs, the system helps leadership prioritize capital investments and build smarter budgets across their portfolio.

Together, these platforms create a unified AI Operational Intelligence System for Hotels, giving ownership groups, management companies, and property teams real-time visibility into operations, guest experience, and asset performance.

OpsTechPro helps hotel organizations reduce labor, improve operational efficiency, protect asset value, and make smarter decisions across every property in their portfolio.

Different shift. Different result.
Same standards. Same training.
Still inconsistent.

Most hotels don’t have a standards problem.
They have an execution problem.

When standards live in binders, PDFs, SharePoint, or tribal knowledge, execution varies—by shift, department, and tenure.

Yipy exists to fix that.

Yipy is the creator of the Hospitality Standards Management System (HSMS)—a new operational system designed to close the Execution Gap.

Because more standards, more audits, and more training don’t solve inconsistency.
They often make it worse.

The problem isn’t effort. It’s where standards live.

Standards that live outside the workflow don’t survive the workflow.

That leads to:

Fragmented systems and manual work
Low confidence in operational data
Delayed feedback that misses the moment
Inconsistent guest experiences

At the same time, guest expectations are rising.
Review scores now function like a conversion rate—small changes drive measurable revenue impact.

The solution: make standards executable.

Yipy installs a living execution system that turns standards into daily performance.

We call this The Consistency Dividend:

Define → Distribute → Deliver → Diagnose → Develop

In practice, Yipy enables:

One living source of truth for standards
Standards delivered at the point of work
QA that becomes daily coaching—not inspection
Real-time visibility across teams and properties

What leaders manage changes:

Minutes-to-feedback
Coaching frequency
Rework rate
Execution variance

Trusted by high-expectation operators

Used by teams at Leading Hotels of the World, The Ritz-Carlton, JW Marriott, Radisson, and independent luxury hotels.

Operators use Yipy to stabilize execution, improve manager effectiveness, and deliver more consistent guest experiences—reflected in reviews, loyalty, and revenue.

Follow Yipy for insights on closing the Execution Gap

With smart tools like a unified inbox, guest app, and automated cleaning management, it’s purpose-built by property managers to help you scale easier. 

Our platform spans three core solution areas: 

Guest Journey 
Deliver seamless stays from booking to checkout. 

1. Unified AI inbox: consolidates all messages from OTAs, WhatsApp, E-mail and direct booking website in one place. 
 
2. Automated Messaging: configure personalized messages triggered by conditions such as length of stay, booking lead time, or channel. Send the right communication at the right moment, from booking confirmations to check-in instructions and beyond. 
 
3. Guest App: a personalized web app created for each reservation. That gives your guests all the information they need in one place, reducing questions and enhancing the overall stay experience by controlling the IoT devices in the room (smart lights, locks, A/C, ..). 
 
4. Review Center: a centralized dashboard designed that allows you to track the performance of your properties and answer guest reviews efficiently. 
 

Smart Operations 
Put your operations on autopilot. 

1. Multi-Calendar View: manage all listings, reservations, and cleaning schedules in one clear, consolidated calendar. 
 
2. IoT Integrations: control smart locks, climate, and energy systems, all from one place. 
 
3. Cleaning Management: automate scheduling, reduce errors, and keep teams in sync in real time. 
 
4. AI Operations Center (coming soon): proactively detect, prevent & resolve issues . 
 

Business Intelligence 
Our built-in analytics provide real-time insights into performance, pricing strategies, guest behavior, and operational trends.

Yipy is the creator of the Hospitality Standards Management System (HSMS)—a new operational system designed to close the Execution Gap.

Because more standards, more audits, and more training don’t solve inconsistency.
They often make it worse.

The problem isn’t effort. It’s where standards live.

Standards that live outside the workflow don’t survive the workflow.

That leads to:

Fragmented systems and manual work
Low confidence in operational data
Delayed feedback that misses the moment
Inconsistent guest experiences

At the same time, guest expectations are rising.
Review scores now function like a conversion rate—small changes drive measurable revenue impact.

The solution: make standards executable.

Yipy installs a living execution system that turns standards into daily performance.

We call this The Consistency Dividend:

Define → Distribute → Deliver → Diagnose → Develop

In practice, Yipy enables:

One living source of truth for standards
Standards delivered at the point of work
QA that becomes daily coaching—not inspection
Real-time visibility across teams and properties

What leaders manage changes:

Minutes-to-feedback
Coaching frequency
Rework rate
Execution variance

Trusted by high-expectation operators

Used by teams at Leading Hotels of the World, The Ritz-Carlton, JW Marriott, Radisson, and independent luxury hotels.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B benchmark.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.

Definition - a company lookalike API takes a seed company and returns other
companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

  ANCHOR       - who the seed sells to, and what it fundamentally is
                 (e.g. "restaurant point-of-sale platform"). This is a HARD
                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.
  When you cannot tell what the candidate sells, anchor_match is false.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).
  List the SEED capabilities this candidate also does, copying the strings
  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.

STEP 3 - relevant.
  relevant = anchor_match AND capabilities_matched is non-empty.
  Nothing else changes it.

Rules that apply throughout:
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. A smaller, larger, or
    differently-located company clears the anchor if it is the same kind of
    company for the same kind of customer. Ignore such metadata.
  - A shared generic taxonomy label or keyword is not an anchor match. Neither
    is a similar technology stack - tech co-signals may support a judgement but
    never establish one.
  - Judge the candidate's primary business, not a side feature.
  - When in doubt on the anchor, answer false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words: name the anchor verdict and the overlap.

Worked examples (SEED anchor -> candidate -> verdict):
  - "restaurant point-of-sale platform" [payments, online ordering, payroll]
      • a restaurant POS suite with payments and online ordering
        -> anchor true, matched [payments, online ordering], relevant true.
      • a restaurant POS with none of the listed capabilities
        -> anchor true, matched [], relevant FALSE (no overlap).
      • a retail-only POS with payments
        -> anchor FALSE (different customer), relevant false.
      • a general payments processor with no restaurant POS product
        -> anchor FALSE (different category), relevant false.
      • an actual restaurant chain
        -> anchor FALSE (customer of the category), relevant false.
      • an agency that installs restaurant POS systems
        -> anchor FALSE (serves the category), relevant false.
  - "CRM and marketing automation platform for go-to-market teams"
      • a smaller CRM with marketing automation -> anchor true, relevant true.
      • a lead-generation agency using that CRM for clients -> anchor false.
  - "digital bank for consumers"
      • a digital bank in another country -> anchor true (geography is not a
        constraint), relevant true if any capability overlaps.
  - "developer-security platform"
      • a company on a similar cloud stack selling HR software -> anchor false.

                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for

    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category

    - A different category fails, even for the same customer

      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).

companies that resemble it. Resemblance has two halves, and they are judged
DIFFERENTLY:

                 requirement. Every lookalike must be the same kind of company
                 for the same kind of customer. No amount of feature overlap
                 substitutes for it.
  CAPABILITIES - what the seed does (e.g. payments, online ordering, payroll,
                 operations). A lookalike matches ANY non-empty subset. It does
                 not need all of them, and matching more is not required to
                 qualify - only to be a closer match.

So: a true lookalike clears the ANCHOR and shares at least one CAPABILITY.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company - the company the lookalike search started from, with its
    ANCHOR and its CAPABILITIES listed separately.
  • A CANDIDATE company - a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide in this order, and do not work backwards from a conclusion:

STEP 1 - anchor_match (the gate).
  True only if the CANDIDATE is the same kind of company as the ANCHOR, for
  the same kind of customer. Ask: would someone shopping for the SEED consider
  this company to be in the same market?
    - A different customer fails, even in the same product category
      (restaurant POS vs retail-only POS: the customer differs).
    - A different category fails, even for the same customer
      (a restaurant POS vs a restaurant-supply distributor: both sell to
      restaurants, but only one is the same kind of company).
    - Serving the category rather than competing in it fails: agencies,
      consultancies, integrators, resellers.
    - Being a customer of the category fails (an actual restaurant is not a
      lookalike of a restaurant POS platform).
    - Parent/holding companies, the seed itself, and duplicate or parody
      entries fail.

STEP 2 - capabilities_matched (the overlap).

  verbatim from the SEED's list. Include a capability when the candidate
  plausibly offers it as part of its product; leave it out when you have no
  evidence. Matching a subset is normal and expected.
